ctx.x: musicians, "There's the old Chief. Let's play Some Day" for the old Chief." And he played "Some Day." At that time Trummy Young was with him. This is a few months later that I get a call from Arvell Shaw who was with Louie and, "Chief, Chief," so he said, "Go to Glaser, they want you in the band!" I said, "Oh, they do, how wonderful, that's nice." "Go to see Joe Glaser." I said, "What about Trummy, isn't he with you any more." He said, "Trummy is in Hawaii, he left for Hawaii, he wants to go home. He didn't give…

And at a later time I heard that that they were after Vic Dickenson, too. But Joe Glaser said, "No, no, no, I don't want Vic Dickenson, he got no personality. Get me Chief. Get me Chief." So Arvell decided he would call me and get in touch with me.

items.title: 67395_Vic Dickenson oral history interview
items.q: Oh, yeah, they got Big Chief.

ctx.x: It was Big Chief right after that.
Oh, yeah, they got Big Chief. He played good.
Oh, sure. I saw him at some point when they had a Lester Lanin band, and there he was.
